previous_description: A constraint specifying how selection of a partition value in one field affects valid or available partition values in another field, enabling combinatorial test design to avoid invalid input combinations per IEEE 829-2008 test design specification.
definition: A cross-field constraint in combinatorial test design stating that when a specific partition value (the trigger) is selected in one InputSpacePartition, the availability of named partition values in another input field is excluded, required, restricted, or re-ranged, so that generated combinations omit invalid inputs.

distinguish_from.when: the condition bounds a single field's own equivalence class (its constraintExpression) and does not depend on the value chosen for any other field.

the restriction is a per-CoverageRequirement choice of which values of one partition to cover or exclude (coverValues/excludeValues), not a rule that applies whenever another field takes a given value.
you are describing the input dimension itself and its presenceRule (including a plain 'conditional' flag), rather than the specific trigger value and affected values that make it conditional.
a target or requirement is deliberately removed from coverage with an approver and accepted risk, rather than a combination being logically invalid.

standard_reference: IEEE 829-2008 Level Test Design Specification (test design refinements: feature/input combinations to be tested); conceptually the category-partition method's selector constraints (Ostrand & Balcer)
code_evidence: A constraint line in a combinatorial test model file, e.g. a PICT/ACTS model containing 'IF [PaymentMethod] = "invoice" THEN [Country] IN {"DE","AT"};'

A parametrized test generator (e.g. pytest_generate_tests, JUnit ArgumentsProvider, itertools.product filter) that drops or skips tuples when one parameter has a specific value and another has a listed value
A property-based test calling assume()/filter() that ties one generated argument's allowed values to another argument's value, e.g. 'assume(not (account_type == "guest" and role == "admin"))'

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text explanation of the business or technical reason the trigger value constrains the affected values (e.g. 'guest accounts cannot hold admin role'); set whenever the rule is not self-evident from effect and affectedValues.

notes: No attribute identifies the dependent (affected) InputSpacePartition or field; affectedValues as bare labels is ambiguous when labels repeat across partitions — add affectedPartitionRef. 'modifies-range' is undefined and overlaps 'restricts-to'. The 'triggers' edge to coveragerequirement and 'constrained-by' to inputpartitionselection have unclear semantics/direction. dependsOnValue duplicates the triggers→partitionvalue edge.
